key_insight: Shear-induced depletion and alignment in bacterial flows are unified as manifestations of a single active phase-space topology.
engineering_relevance: This research provides a predictive framework for understanding bacterial transport in low-Reynolds-number flows, improving engineering designs in microfluidic systems.
method: Developed an analytical hydrodynamic model from first principles.
Utilized the method of images to characterize flow-wall coupling.
evidence_signal: The model quantitatively reproduces measured bacterial distributions validated against microfluidic experiments.
watch_item: Potential challenges in extrapolating findings to more complex biological systems or varying environmental conditions.
paper_title: Active phase-space topology unifies depletion and alignment in bacterial flows
